groups.notes: First calibration of this group: six eligible small units from root feature #82, all Markdown-authoring work against a shared documentation invariant test seam in a Rust repository (agent-skill documentation, not Rust code implementation) — a narrow work class that must not be generalised to Rust code changes generally. All six started and finished cleanly on claude:claude-sonnet-5/low (ladderIndex 0): zero capability escalations, zero material review-driven fix passes. #84's one fix pass was excluded from materialReReview because its own notes record it as ordinary TDD self-correction found by the unit's own test step, not review-driven. #88's first review pass was discarded as an invalidated dispatch (stdin-blocked reviewer leaves), not a review result; its recorded pass (r1b) was clean. #93 shows acceptancePassed:false, but its own notes attribute this to two acceptance criteria that were unsatisfiable by construction (documenting a CLI flag the real binary variant does not accept) — a defect in the issue, not in the model's capability — so it is counted as a clean model-routing success. Recommendation retained at claude:claude-sonnet-5/low: index 0 is already the verified floor, so no further lowering or boundary probe below it is possible, and six-of-six clean at the floor is exactly the kind of evidence the lowering threshold asks for, it just has nowhere lower to go. The Claude subagent adapter exposes model but not effort, so effort reads 'unknown' on every attempt here; this group's evidence is model-axis only and must not be read as saying anything about effort steps. No usage/cost/token/duration figures were reported by the harness for any attempt in any of the twelve #83-94 units, so costToAcceptance falls back to attempt count (unit: attempts) with confidence low, per the rubric's fallback order.

groups.notes: First calibration of this group: six eligible medium units from root feature #82, the same narrow Markdown-authoring-against-a-shared-test-seam work class as the sibling small group, not general Rust code implementation. Only #89 was clean on the first pass. #85 is the run's one model-dimension escalation: after two valid material non-clean review passes with the same failure mode (unqualified safety absolutes in prose), the implementer moved from claude:claude-sonnet-5/low to claude:claude-opus-5, skipping the usual same-model effort escalation step because the Claude subagent adapter exposes no effort control to raise first (effort reads 'unknown' on every attempt in this run) — so this is model-axis evidence only, and no effort-axis conclusion can be drawn from it. One escalated unit is short of the rubric's two-comparable-unit threshold for raising the floor, so the recommendation is retained at claude:claude-sonnet-5/low rather than raised to opus-5; this is recorded as evidence to watch, not as a floor change. #83, #90, #91, and #94 each required one or more review-driven fix passes without any route escalation: #90, #91, and #94 had findings the reviewer upheld and the implementer fixed at the same route; #83's two Spec findings were themselves adjudicated as a rejected interpretive claim (a maintainer-reversible reading, not a code defect) even though the unit still consumed two review passes and a fix pass, so #83 is counted toward materialReReview's attempt cost but is explicitly not capability-escalation evidence — separating the code fact from the interpretive spec reading per this team's own review practice. Net signal: this work class shows a materially higher re-review rate than its small-sized sibling group (5 of 6 vs 0 of 6), but because only one of those five re-reviews actually required a stronger route, the evidence supports 'expect more turns at this size' rather than 'start higher for this size'. No usage/cost/token/duration figures were reported by the harness for any attempt in any of the twelve #83-94 units, so costToAcceptance falls back to attempt count (unit: attempts) with confidence low.
